question: Can role_host.py run each Pi turn in a container whose only route out is a host egress proxy, with the host's own tools, no credentials inside, and a verified codebase-memory index?
n: 1 per cell; one machine; every provider request went to tests/role_host_fakes/fake_openai_responses.py; no provider was contacted

facts.fact: Host Pi 1.4.0 runs unmodified in the pinned image from the snap tree bind-mounted read-only (node v22.23.4 in the image, Pi needs >=22.19); its only native addon is the TUI X11 one.

With host /usr and /etc bind-mounted read-only, the container reports the host user (bline), git 2.53.0 and Python 3.14.4; host home content is absent unless mounted; host environment variables are not inherited.
Docker's --init cannot be injected with host /usr mounted read-only (/sbin/docker-init not found); the entry script runs as PID 1, forwards SIGTERM/SIGINT to Pi and reaps orphans.
A tmpfs at the host home path with read-only binds beneath it works; same-path mounts keep Pi's session file and paths identical to the host.
strace can trace its own child under cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges and the default seccomp profile; attaching to a non-descendant is refused, as on the host (ptrace_scope 1).

An --internal Docker network still reaches the host: TCP to its bridge address 172.20.0.1 was refused by the host, and host UDP services bind every bridge address (3702, 5353). All 17 host TCP listeners were loopback-only.
--network none leaves only lo: TCP to 1.1.1.1, the docker0 gateway and the LAN address, and UDP to the host's 3702, all fail with ENETUNREACH.

A relay in the container from 127.0.0.1:8080 to a mounted Unix socket reaches a host proxy; Pi's openai provider with baseUrl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 completed turns through it. The container sent only a placeholder key and the proxy substituted its own.

Through role_host --container, the agent's own bash (driven by a fake function call) saw: 'Network is unreachable', the unmounted folder absent, OPENAI_API_KEY equal to the placeholder, host git 2.53.0, a --mount-ro file readable and writes to it refused with 'Read-only file system'.

The proxy observed the requested tier on the provider's terminal event for every request; a shell request to the proxy for another model, a hosted tool, another path or beyond --max-requests was refused without reaching the upstream.

docker stop -t 10 ends a turn in about 0.1-0.5 s (Pi exits on the forwarded SIGTERM). A hard-killed attached docker run client leaves its container running, so turns run detached and write events to a mounted directory.

codebase-memory indexes into a custom CBM_CACHE_DIR without touching the shared cache. Its runtime dir must already exist and keep the coordination socket path within 108 bytes; under a long state path it failed with 'secure CLI coordination could not be created (endpoint)'. A short host temp dir and a container tmpfs at /run/cbm work.

Inside the container, index_status for the session's fresh index reported status ready and root_path equal to the working directory; Pi offered 17 codebase-memory tools with exposure direct, named mcp__codebase_memory_mcp__<tool>; a model call to search_graph returned the indexed function. Pi's default exposure is codemode (not declared to the model).
A later turn after a mounted folder was removed was refused with environment_changed.

source_facts: docker secret needs Swarm (this node is inactive); non-Swarm secrets are mounted files readable by every process in the container, including Pi's bash tool.

Pi honours HTTP(S)_PROXY through undici EnvHttpProxyAgent and an httpProxy setting (dist/core/http-dispatcher.js); a CONNECT proxy would leave the key in the container and the tier invisible to the proxy.

Pi's openai-codex provider derives the account id from the token and may use WebSocket; host Pi prints live credentials with `pi auth print-api-key` and `pi auth print-bearer-token --min-expiry` (not run for openai-codex: the owner reported its quota at 0%).
